ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Okafor, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
New-onset headache and scalp tenderness for two weeks with transient visual disturbances

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 77-year-old female with polymyalgia rheumatica presenting with new-onset headache and scalp tenderness after prior evaluation for cognitive decline in 2020. The pain is localized to her right temporal region and is described as a constant, dull ache. She reports associated jaw discomfort when chewing, as well as generalized fatigue and weight loss. Over the past few days, she has also noticed transient blurring of vision in her right eye.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Major depressive disorder (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hypertension
- Osteoporosis
- Polymyalgia rheumatica
- Hyperlipidemia
- Osteoarthritis (bilateral knees)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Total abdominal hysterectomy (age 52)
- Right cataract extraction with posterior chamber IOL (age 74)
- Left total knee arthroplasty (age 71)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Amlodipine 5 mg oral daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg oral nightly
- Prednisone 5 mg oral daily
- Alendronate 70 mg oral weekly
- Calcium carbonate/Vitamin D3 600 mg-400 units oral twice daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for pain

ALLERGIES:
Sulfonamides (diffuse maculopapular rash), Latex (contact dermatitis)

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, hip fracture
- Father: Coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction (age 78)
- Sister: Major depressive disorder, hypothyroidism
- Maternal grandmother: Temporal arteritis (late onset)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1-2 glasses wine on holidays). Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, there is tenderness over the right temple with decreased pulsation of the right temporal artery.
Neurological examination is otherwise unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
The patient's erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) is markedly elevated at 85 mm/hr.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Internal Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the clinic by her daughter due to worsening memory and reduced functioning over the past 3 months

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The daughter reports that her mother often sits silently, avoids social interactions, and has stopped preparing meals, which she previously enjoyed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Hypertension
- Osteoporosis
- Polymyalgia rheumatica
- Hyperlipidemia
- Osteoarthritis (bilateral knees)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Total abdominal hysterectomy (age 52)
- Right cataract extraction with posterior chamber IOL (age 74)
- Left total knee arthroplasty (age 71)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Amlodipine 5 mg oral daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg oral nightly
- Prednisone 5 mg oral daily
- Alendronate 70 mg oral weekly
- Calcium carbonate/Vitamin D3 600 mg-400 units oral twice daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for pain

ALLERGIES:
Sulfonamides (diffuse maculopapular rash), Latex (contact dermatitis)

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, hip fracture
- Father: Coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction (age 78)
- Sister: Major depressive disorder, hypothyroidism
- Maternal grandmother: Temporal arteritis (late onset)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1-2 glasses wine on holidays). Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
During the interview, the patient maintains minimal eye contact, speaks in a soft voice, and gives brief answers. She is unable to recall any of three words after 5 minutes and makes no attempt to guess. When asked to draw a clock, she initially refuses, but completes it correctly with encouragement. Physical examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Basic labs are unremarkable
